windows.reason: The obstacle is the Windows ROCm toolchain, not the GPU and not the port. lc0's value head is wrong by ~4.4e-02 absolute (relative 4.9e-01, with sign flips) against a 1e-3/1e-2 bar, while the policy head is bit-identical (~3e-07). The defect reproduces IDENTICALLY on all three Windows architectures tested -- gfx1151, gfx1101 and gfx1201 -- while linux-gfx90a (wave64) AND linux-gfx1100 (wave32) both PASS the same check at the same head. gfx1100 has the same wavefront width as gfx1151, so this is not a wave-size effect; the only variable that tracks the failure is the operating system and its ROCm/rocBLAS build. A prior exhaustive investigation cleared the obvious candidates: graph capture disabled, use_gemm_ex=false, Conv1Layer loop replacement, and standalone BLAS tests at the relevant dimensions all PASS. Leading suspicion is a gfx-specific rocBLAS/Tensile fallback kernel for the value head's small GEMM shapes in TheRock's Windows SDK. RE-CONFIRMED 2026-08-20 at head 7727fa3 on a NEWER SDK (TheRock ROCm 7.14.0a20260612, clang 23.0.0git) than the original 2026-06-04 ruling (7.14.0a20260604): 261/261 targets built, CPU gtest 8/8, benchmark fault-free, and the check backend still reports 0/222 passing with the identical 4.4e-02 magnitude and pattern. NOTE for the approver: the alternative to a waiver is a toolchain bug report against TheRock's rocBLAS rather than any change to this port. Jeff Daily already ruled BLOCK-and-move-on on 2026-06-04; this suggestion only offers the waiver route to close the record.

windows-gfx1101.blocked_reason: Value-head numerical defect identical to gfx1151: builds+runs (344 targets, benchmark clean, 8/8 CPU gtest), policy bit-identical (~4.6e-07) but value wrong 4.4e-02 absolute (sign flips) at atol=1e-3 bar. Defect appears identically on gfx1201 under same TheRock ROCm 7.14 Windows SDK. Exhaustive investigation: graph capture off, use_gemm_ex=false, Conv1Layer loop replacement, standalone BLAS tests all PASS -- BLAS is correct for all relevant dimensions. Root cause unresolved; suspected TheRock ROCm 7.14 Windows HIP runtime issue in custom kernel path. Linux gfx90a+gfx1100 pass the same check on ROCm 7.2.1.

windows-gfx1201.blocked_reason: Value-head numerical defect identical to gfx1151 and gfx1101: builds+runs (344 targets, benchmark clean, 8/8 CPU gtest), policy bit-identical (~4.6e-07) but value wrong 4.4e-02 absolute (sign flips) at atol=1e-3 bar. Defect appears identically on gfx1101 under same TheRock ROCm 7.14 Windows SDK. Exhaustive investigation: graph capture off, use_gemm_ex=false, Conv1Layer loop replacement, standalone BLAS tests all PASS -- BLAS is correct for all relevant dimensions. Root cause unresolved; suspected TheRock ROCm 7.14 Windows HIP runtime issue in custom kernel path. Linux gfx90a+gfx1100 pass the same check on ROCm 7.2.1.

windows-gfx1151.blocked_reason: Value-head numerical defect confirmed unchanged at head 7727fa3 on TheRock ROCm 7.14.0a20260612 Windows SDK (AMD clang 23.0.0git). Builds+runs clean (261/261 targets, 8/8 CPU gtest, benchmark batch 1-256 fault-free). maia-1100 check backend (hip vs blas, atol=1e-3 rtol=1e-2): policy bit-identical (abs 3.0e-07, rel 5.2e-06); value wrong (abs 4.4e-02, rel 4.9e-01) on every one of 222/222 batches (sizes 1-55). Identical magnitude and pattern to the 2026-06-04 gfx1151 block and the 2026-06-05 gfx1101/gfx1201 block. Root cause unresolved (prior exhaustive investigation on gfx1101/gfx1201: graph capture off, use_gemm_ex=false, Conv1Layer loop replacement, standalone BLAS tests all PASS -- BLAS correct). Reopen if a TheRock ROCm Windows HIP runtime or value-head kernel fix is identified.
